coverage.notes: Evergreen publishes roughly four weeks ahead, not eight. A second pass with the departure date moved to 12 Oct returned a single sailing on CNSHA-USNYC, which confirms the horizon rather than extending it, so Evergreen coverage of this window is weeks 38 to about 42 and weeks 43 to 45 rest on Hapag, MSC and ONE alone. Hapag was queried twice per lane (start dates 14 Sep and 20 Oct) and MSC twice per lane (14 Sep and 12 Oct) to span the full window; ONE was queried once per lane at nextWeekValue 56 and never hit its session ceiling - the "Thanks for Your Patience" string was tested on every lane and was false throughout. Cai Mep resolves to different codes per carrier: VNVUU on Evergreen, VNVUT on Hapag and MSC. ONE rejected VNCMT, VNVUT and its own autocomplete, so the three ONE Cai Mep lanes were not covered. Maersk contributed vessel-level verification only and no lane sweep, and CMA CGM contributed nothing this run. Flexport Atlas sat behind a Cloudflare interstitial for roughly half a minute on first load but cleared on its own; both TEU figures were re-queried successfully, so no TEU in this file is stale.

alerts.detail: No first sighting this run. All three published items reappeared with rotations and dates identical to the 13 Sep capture, so there is no EXTRA LOADER DETECTED, no EXTRA LOADER UPDATED and no EXTRA LOADER GONE. OGEC EVER LASTING 0021-097E was re-read straight off the Evergreen vessel schedule and matched all eleven port pairs. AA9 WAN HAI 903 E002 matched all ten. XL MAERSK MONTANA 639E matched all five. No new OGEC voyage number has appeared: Evergreen still shows only 0021 for EVER LASTING and 0020 for TRITON, and TRITON 0020-048E sailed Yantian on 04 Sep, ISO week 36, so it stays in history.

Hapag CNYTN-USNYC returned AA7 5 with isGemini false and US4 6 with isGemini true and flagged nothing, exactly as the regression baseline requires. Evergreen CNYTN-USNYC returned SAX 3, AUE 3 and CBX 5 and flagged nothing. Evergreen CNNGB-USNYC returned NUE2 4, NUE 3 and OGEC 1 and flagged OGEC only. Across 179 in-window Hapag sailings, 142 MSC and 12 ONE lanes, the only service codes seen were registry codes or codes already on the deny list.

AUG and EC4 are the same string. The detector flagged AUG as unknown on CNSHA-USHOU at n 1 because it was checking the registry printed in the task file rather than the registry stored here, where AUG was already promoted. The cross-check settles it independently: Evergreen sells CONTI CORTESIA 014E, ONE ARCADIA 079E and EVER LUCKY 085E as AUG, and ONE sells ONE ARCADIA 079E and EVER LUCKY 085E on the same lane as EC4. The Evergreen vessel schedule names it verbatim as "Asia-U.S. GULF Service(AUG)" and shows a westbound 085W round-trip leg, so it is a fixed proforma service and not an extra loader. Worth folding AUG to EC4 in the alias map next time the registry is edited.

HTW added. It surfaced three times on Evergreen VNTOT-USHOU (EVER MACH 1472-018E, EVER MOST 1474-011E, EVER MAGUS 1476-009E) as the first leg of a transhipment routing, which is an intra-Asia feeder and not Gulf coverage. NSB, KTH, FP2 and OGME were seen again and were already on the list. OGME is Evergreen ad-hoc but Middle East, so it is correctly out of scope.

CMA CGM. The routing finder resolved both ports but the Search button collapsed to a zero-size bounding box once the period field was set, and no routing request was issued at all. DataDome was never reached, so the quota shared with the market-refresh task was not touched. Re-test next run.

Maersk point-to-point. One interactive search succeeded, then the geography locations API began returning 400 for every query and the routings-queries replay returned 422 because the Akamai telemetry token is single-use. The vessel-schedule endpoint stayed open and was used to re-verify MAERSK MONTANA 639E including TEU and IMO, so the published Maersk item is fully current; what is missing is the ability to find a NEW Maersk extra loader this run.

Lanes not covered this run: all fifteen CMA CGM lanes; all fifteen Maersk point-to-point lanes; ONE VNCMT-USNYC, VNCMT-USSAV and VNCMT-USHOU. Evergreen covered all fifteen but only to about week 42 because Evergreen publishes roughly four weeks ahead, so weeks 43 to 45 of this window rest on Hapag, MSC and ONE. Everything else in scope was queried: Evergreen 15, Hapag 18, MSC 15, ONE 12, plus four vessel-level lookups and two Wan Hai service CSVs.

Independents not scanned (out of scope): SeaLead, TS Lines, Emirates, CU Lines, Transfar, Matson and similar. Ad-hoc capacity from these carriers is not reflected here. This is the largest known gap in the report and it is unchanged from every previous run.

All three published TEU figures were re-queried this run rather than carried forward. EVER LASTING 9,466 TEU and WAN HAI 903 8,700 TEU from Flexport Atlas by IMO, MAERSK MONTANA 4,544 TEU from Maersk own vessel particulars. All three unchanged. Atlas needed about 30 seconds to clear a Cloudflare interstitial on the first request; it cleared without intervention and the second lookup was immediate.
